subject: Console beta: Model changelog tab (select accounts) — rollout + rollback plan
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2026 at 4:03 PM
Subject: Console beta: Model changelog tab (select accounts) — rollout + rollback plan

Chloe / Jada — looping you both in so we can turn on a limited Console beta for the customer-visible model changelog.

Goal: enable the “Changelog” tab on model + version pages for a small set of accounts next week (behind a feature flag + tier gate). This is coming up in a few enterprise conversations and I’d like us to have something we can safely show.

Proposed beta accounts (initial):
- FinchBank (security/procurement heavy)
- StackForge (devtools, wants transparency + pinning)
- HelioHealth (regulated change approvals)

Assumptions (please correct):
- Read-only view in Console (no editing from UI)
- Entries shown must be in PUBLISHED state only
- Console should never render internal-only metadata fields (only what’s in public allowlist)

Risks I want us to explicitly cover before flipping it on:
1) Incorrect / confusing note gets published and immediately visible in Console
2) Docs links (changelog_url) 404 or lag behind publication
3) Any accidental leakage (internal model nicknames, vendor provenance, internal eval IDs, etc.)
4) Pagination/filter semantics lead to missing entries and support confusion

Rollback / backout requirements:
- Ability to disable via flag instantly (no deploy)
- If we publish a bad entry, we need a “supersede/correct” path that preserves audit history (not silent edit)
- If docs sync lags, Console should degrade gracefully (show entry text + “Docs link pending” vs broken link)

Can you both reply with:
- What flag / gating we’ll use (name + where it’s enforced)
- What we consider “go/no-go” checks for the beta
- A concrete rollback plan + who’s on point if we have to back it out

I’d like to align by EOD today so we can schedule the flag enable early next week.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Sponsor, Console/Control Plane
Redwood Inference


---

From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2026 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Console beta: Model changelog tab (select accounts) — rollout + rollback plan

Yep — we can do this safely with a strict read-only surface.

Flag/gating proposal:
- Feature flag: console.model_changelog_beta
- Enforced in Console backend (not just UI) so direct calls from the UI won’t work if disabled
- Allowlist on account_id (we can also optionally add min tier = Enterprise, but I’d prefer explicit allowlist for beta)

Behavior:
- Console backend will only query entries where state=PUBLISHED
- We’ll hard-fail if the response includes any fields outside the public allowlist (defensive: prevents accidentally rendering new fields)
- If changelog_url is null or returns non-200, we show the Console-rendered entry only (no outbound link)

Go/no-go checks I suggest:
1) Staging: verify pagination/filtering works with seeded data across 20+ entries
2) Staging: force docs link failure and confirm UI behavior (no 404 exposure)
3) Verify caching headers / ETags are correct for the feed endpoint (avoids Console hammering)
4) Confirm rate limits won’t impact those accounts

Rollback:
- Flip flag off (instant)
- If any issue is content-related (bad note), we use the correction flow (supersede) and keep the flag on if the product surface is fine
- If the issue is leakage-risk: flag off immediately, then we hotfix allowlist/templating before re-enabling

Owner for rollback page:
- I can be primary for backend issues; Ethan/Control Plane can help if it’s upstream API behavior.

One more note: if we’re depending on docs-site being current, we should treat docs as “best-effort” in beta and keep Console as source of rendered content.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Console Backend Lead


---

From: Jada Williams <jada@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2026 at 5:12 PM
Subject: Re: Console beta: Model changelog tab (select accounts) — rollout + rollback plan

+1 to Chloe’s plan.

Workflow / approval notes:
- Console beta should only surface entries in PUBLISHED.
- Draft -> in_review -> published transitions are already permissioned via the release-note publication roles (separate from model metadata edit roles).
- For beta, I recommend we keep the emergency path documented but restricted:
  - “Emergency publish” (skip parts of review) only for Connor O’Brien + Marissa (product) + one eng approver (Dylan as sponsor). Everyone else goes through normal in_review.

Rollback from a workflow perspective:
- If published content is wrong/confusing: publish a corrected entry that supersedes the previous one (do NOT edit in place).
- If content includes something it shouldn’t (policy/security): flag off + publish correction immediately; we also need a checklist item that Support is notified before re-enable.

Go/no-go checks (workflow side):
1) Confirm audit events show: actor, timestamp, event_id, previous_state->new_state
2) Confirm correction/supersede preserves history and is visible in Console as “Superseded by …”
3) Validate RBAC mappings in the beta environment (no accidental broad access)

If helpful I can write up a short “beta operating mode” doc (who can publish, who on call, and what to do when an enterprise asks for an export).

— Jada
Jada Williams
Workflow Architect


---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>, Jada Williams <jada@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2026 at 6:01 PM
Subject: Re: Console beta: Model changelog tab (select accounts) — rollout + rollback plan

This is exactly what I needed.

Let’s do:
- Flag: console.model_changelog_beta
- Gate: explicit account allowlist in backend
- Display: published-only; Console-rendered content is the primary surface; docs link optional

Go/no-go checklist (final):
1) Staging leak test: new/unexpected fields cause hard failure (no render)
2) Staging docs failure test: no broken links shown
3) Audit verification: publish + supersede produce correct audit events
4) Smoke test on one internal test account before enabling 3 beta accounts

Rollback plan:
- Leakage risk: flag off immediately (owner: Chloe), then fix allowlist/templating; re-enable only after Marissa sign-off
- Content issue: publish correction/supersede (owner: Jada to coordinate workflow; Marissa final wording sign-off)

Chloe — can you confirm ETA for wiring the account allowlist + defensive allowlist failure behavior?
Jada — please draft the “beta operating mode” doc (short is fine) and include the emergency publish constraint you outlined.

If we hit all checks Monday, I’m comfortable enabling for FinchBank/StackForge/HelioHealth Tuesday AM.

— Dylan

ETA:
- Account allowlist enforcement + fail-closed on unknown fields: I can have it in staging by Monday 11am.
- If tests pass, production-ready same day (no schema changes required).

I’ll also add a simple dashboard panel for:
- % requests blocked by flag/gate
- changelog endpoint error rate
- docs link resolution failures (if we have the signal)

— Chloe
